name: naive-thresholding
title: Pairwise thresholds no report can print
idea: Thresholding each pair on its own leaves triples of firms that no grade report can print; the card's grade blocks repair them by withholding some confident pairs and stating some doubtful ones.
from: new angle · v1 S-02 heat map, second stage (pairs past the threshold), and KRW section V.E (naive thresholding); adds the unprintable triples among the 97 firms (including two pairs left unsaid with the third stated; the race baseline has no strict 3-cycles, while the signed gender target has one at λ=1), their change with λ and their overlap with the card's blocks
credit: After Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), section V.E, and the postrank theory book, ch. 10. Firms as adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (pr_case_krw). Cards computed with KRW's code (KRW replication companion) under KRW's archived pair probabilities.
caption: Strict isolated pair thresholds on the released KRW law, compared with the current archived card; shared grades make no equality claim.
